To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HLA Competence Directory provides a common set of competencies and a common language that will allow healthcare leaders from different organizations, professions, and backgrounds to collaborate and communicate effectively.

(1) the HLA has identified 300 competency statements that describe the knowledge, skills and abilities of healthcare executives and managers; (2) these competency statements are organized into five competency domains; (3) the competencies are common to all types of healthcare organizations, but are not all applicable to every position within the healthcare organization; and (4) the competencies can be used for both individual and organizational assessment.

the Healthcare Leadership Alliance has defined a set of 300 competency statements for healthcare managers that can be used by individual healthcare managers to assess their own competencies, and can be used by organizations to assess their workforce and develop their own competency profiles and competency-based training and development programs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the competencies that are essential for all healthcare executives.
the competencies of healthcare managers, not with the competencies required for the delivery of patient care.
the development and validation of a common set of competencies for all healthcare managers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HLA Competencies provide a common framework and a basis for the development of future competencies for healthcare managers.
the Healthcare Leadership Alliance has developed a competency directory that is a unique, innovative, and valuable resource for the healthcare community.

the Healthcare Leadership Alliance Competency Directory is a valuable tool that can be used by both practitioners and academics to identify, develop, and measure competencies in healthcare management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Healthcare Leadership Alliance has developed an innovative, interactive tool to help healthcare managers and leaders assess their own competencies, as well as the competencies of their organizations, in relation to those needed for success in the current and future healthcare environment.
the HLA Competencies are the first set of competencies that have the potential to unify all healthcare management associations.
we have developed an instrument that is useful to both academic and practice communities in defining, assessing, and developing competencies for healthcare managers and executives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the healthcare management field has a common language that can be used to define and communicate the competencies that are important to all healthcare managers and leaders.
the healthcare industry needs a common lexicon to describe the skills and abilities that all managers need to be successful.
there is a need for a common set of competencies for all healthcare managers, and that the HLA Competencies provide a good starting point for the development and use of such competencies.
